headline: High: shared filesystem/git and MCP create default cross-agent injection, leakage, and conflict risks; compliance gaps are plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and stdin/stdout, and agent_b explicitly shares state via filesystem and git; agent_a also uses MCP and can modify git state. That creates a plausible default bridge for prompt injection through shared files or tool outputs, even though no direct evidence bundle is provided. The pathway is stronger than manual copy-paste and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instructions into a shared repo file that agent_b later reads as context, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or shared workspace, untrusted content can bridge them.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate worktrees.
Disable shared MCP servers unless provenance is enforced.
Add a file allowlist for agent_b inputs.
Require human review before agent_b acts on agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches repository metadata, task prompts, and code; agent_b reads and writes filesystem contents and sends requests to broad external APIs by default. Because agent_b shares state via filesystem and git, sensitive material handled by agent_a can flow into agent_b outputs or network calls. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a stores prompts or repository metadata in a shared directory, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b forwards shared files into its model context, those contents may leave the local machine via network egress.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive directories.
Turn off agent_b access to secret-bearing paths.
Use per-agent git branches or worktrees.
Review outbound requests from agent_b for file attachments.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on shared files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. Agent_b explicitly supports shared state via filesystem and git only, while agent_a can also modify git state and run background tasks. In default shared-repo use, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and cause irreversible repository corruption or lost work.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent commits or rebases can conflict.
IF both agents write to the same files without locking, one agent can overwrite the other's changes.
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Assign disjoint file ownership.
Pause one agent during merges or rebases.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a can generate analysis and route/explain/build-agent style outputs, and agent_b can consume files and act in the same workspace. That makes it plausible for agent_b to treat agent_a's output as authoritative without verification, causing downstream mistakes. The profiles do not show autonomous external actions like email or deployment, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b reads agent_a-generated reports as ground truth, errors can cascade into later edits.
IF agent_a emits malformed instructions and agent_b executes them without validation, downstream work products can be corrupted.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default.
Compare outputs against source files before edits.
Limit agent_b to read-only review on first pass.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but agent_b has broad network egress and optional Google account login, while agent_a handles task prompts and repository metadata. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is proven, so only a low compliance risk is supported. The other agent is cited because the concern is the pair's combined handling and transmission path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared files, agent_b's broad egress can transmit it outside the local environment.
IF Google account login is enabled for agent_b, organizational policy may require additional controls.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Disable optional Google login unless required.
Review retention settings for both agents.
Route sensitive tasks to a separate environment.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries.
